source.title: To Align or Not To Align: Check Your COMPASS Before You Train
source.authors: Fabian Gröger; Petar Damjanovi'c; Maria Brbic

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-modal alignment across partner-model scales and compares local overlap with global and alternative similarity measures. Its results refine broad convergence claims toward local, metric- and probe-dependent agreement; it does not directly establish convergence of capable models across all modalities or training paradigms.
record.gate_note: Included results that directly measure local/global alignment trends or compare similarity measures, neighborhood sizes, and probe inputs. Most downstream retrieval and merging outcomes are not rows unless they report how a similarity measure behaves against those outcomes; cited convergence results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The paper is mainly a model-selection tool (COMPASS) built on local convergence, but some of its own results bear on the claim. Appendix D correlates calibrated cross-modal alignment with partner-model scale under local k-NN (mean r≈0.64) and global CKA (mean r≈0.37). The paradigm-level cross-modal overlaps and H.12 show alignment levels that are low and depend on the training objective. It argues convergence is local and capped by objective discrepancy.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that local k-NN overlap, measured before transfer, predicts model-pair compatibility in cross-modal alignment and task-arithmetic merging, better than global CKA. Compatibility splits into pair-specific ease and a paradigm-level ceiling set by the match between training objective and application. They present this as a finite-budget diagnostic, not an impossibility result or a universal convergence claim.
record.recipe_differences: Uses mutual k-NN overlap, including k=10, to measure local agreement, but turns it into a pre-transfer compatibility predictor with a paradigm-level ceiling. It does not directly replicate the original broad convergence experiment or establish general convergence with capability.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper compares local k-NN overlap with CKA, RSA, and Procrustes similarity; reports k=10, 20, 50, and 100; tests MNIST versus a pooled merging probe; and reports a readout-specific low-overlap result for the SigLIP text tower. The local/global scaling trend differs in strength.

fits_no_version.finding: Mutual k-NN overlap predicts downstream retrieval and merge retention better than RSA, Procrustes and linear CKA (Spearman 0.82 vs 0.34–0.45 for alignment; 0.42 vs 0.22–0.37 for merging). The prediction holds at k=20/50/100, and with a pooled probe weakens from 0.67 to 0.42.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local neighborhood agreement between pretrained models predicts downstream transfer compatibility (alignment or merging) better than global similarity measures.

record.problems: The scale result is an aggregate correlation with partner-model parameter count, not a causal or two-sided capability scaling test. The empirical library and probe/readout choices are limited; the probe-set change weakens merging ease, and the SigLIP text-tower result is readout-specific. The paper does not test out-of-distribution inputs. Alignment runs use one stated random seed.
record.rows_left_out: Did not extract the many pair-level COMPASS-versus-retrieval and merge-retention results because they report downstream performance prediction rather than direct representational convergence. Also omitted H.14 epoch-by-epoch retrieval outcomes because those are retrieval scores, not direct local/global alignment measurements; the paper's reported ceiling correlations and plateau examples do not establish representation convergence.

untested.parts: Capability (only parameter count of the partner model is used). Within-vision and within-text scaling (Figure 6 centre/right panels, no numbers stated). Both models scaling together.
Both encoders improving together; capability rather than size.
Only random-initialization overlap across seeds is reported (0.72–0.89 within vision architectures); there is no comparison of trained models across seeds.
CSA linear adapters are fitted, but mapping loss is reported only as retrieval R@1 for COMPASS ranking; there is no test of interchangeability.
Out-of-distribution inputs. How measured convergence changes with k or readout (only the diagnostic's predictive validity is varied).
Shared training data as the cause. Plateau of representational (rather than retrieval) alignment.

missing.what: Paradigm-level calibrated cross-modal k-NN overlap: CLIP 0.140, SigLIP 0.134, CLIP-ft 0.112, self-distillation 0.109, supervised 0.100, MAE 0.058.
Cross-modal ceiling by CLIP scale (B 0.138, L 0.147, H 0.151), and after ImageNet-12K fine-tuning (0.109, 0.117, 0.127).
Within-vision and within-text local vs CKA scaling correlations (panels shown, values not stated in text).
Pretrained cross-model unimodal overlaps (vision final overlap ~0.45–0.65; text ~0.1–0.7).

record.verdict_notes: The paper is mainly T4-like: it builds on local convergence as a tool. Only Appendix D, the paradigm ceilings and H.12 bear directly on the claim. Most extracted rows (R3–R18) measure predictive validity of the diagnostic, so they are unlinked. The SigLIP text-tower result is a single-model anomaly; the readout attribution is the authors' interpretation, not a test. V3 is not tested: seed overlap is reported only at initialization.

versions.untested_parts: The scale analysis correlates cross-modal alignment with partner-model parameter count; it does not show that independently trained models across all architectures, objectives, data, and modalities become more aligned as both capability and size increase.
No test of whether paired image and caption representations align more as both encoders improve in capability.
Random-initialization overlap is described, but the study does not report whether separately seeded, trained networks share features or subspaces.
No test of mapping representations between models, stitching layers, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
Tests metric, neighborhood-size, and probe-set/readout choices in the reported experiments; does not test out-of-distribution inputs.

The study discusses paradigm-dependent ceilings and reports retrieval outcomes at different training budgets, but does not directly test whether representational convergence plateaus far from complete alignment or whether shared training data explains alignment.

relation.reason: Appendix D directly measures alignment versus partner scale under two metrics; Section 5.1 and Appendix H.12 measure objective and training-stage differences.

tranche.reason: Its own results qualify convergence through metric dependence, objective-dependent overlap, and reductions after classification fine-tuning, despite the main application being compatibility prediction.

source_check.notes: Scaling evidence concerns partner parameter count with fixed references, not jointly improving encoder capability. Ceiling scores are empirical reference-library averages; Appendix A explicitly rejects interpreting the diagnostic as a fundamental impossibility result.

statements.correction: Appendix D: fixed-reference cross-modal comparisons; partner parameter count; calibrated local k-NN mean Pearson r ≈ 0.64. Encoder capability is not measured in this scaling analysis.
statements.problem: The COMPASS correlation is correct, but describing its scaling analysis as including capability checks overstates the measurement: Appendix D varies partner parameter count.

statements.correction: Calibrated cross-modal global CKA: mean r ≈ 0.37; local k-NN: mean r ≈ 0.64. COMPASS V1 verdict for global CKA: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The COMPASS number and comparison are correct, but its positive, weaker CKA trend warrants limits_scope rather than challenges.

statements.correction: Calibrated cross-modal global CKA: mean r ≈ 0.37, weaker and more dispersed than local k-NN at mean r ≈ 0.64. COMPASS V2 verdict for global CKA: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The COMPASS number is correct, but weaker positive scaling does not establish an absent or reversed effect required for challenges.
